crime_highlights: Adam Drake discretely, but rapidly and forcefully, stabbed Pat Stay in the chest with the blade of the weapon entering Pat Stay’s heart.
the needless and senseless extinction of the life of a young and contributing member of the community
rationale_highlights: His grandfather is a residential school survivor.
He was the victim of trauma at the hands of persons in authority outside of the household.
Many identifiable systemic discriminatory factors have influenced and plagued his youth and adult life
I have considered the appropriate mitigation related to the Gladue factors
note: Brief statement that Gladue mitigation was applied; 17 years set, below Crown range

crime_highlights: As Patrick Holley continued his rant about the wrongs he had suffered, he threatened to torture his tormentors by pouring boiling grease over their heads in front of their children.
Ms. Hill, upset and somewhat afraid, recruited a court officer to escort her to her car.
rationale_highlights: The Pre-Sentence Report elucidates Patrick Holley’s background including his Aboriginal Status and activities on behalf of his own and other First Nations groups.
The learned trial judge took Patrick Holley’s Aboriginal status into account in determining the nature of the sentence he would impose.
He did not undervalue or give less than warranted influence to the provisions of section 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code.
note: Appeal court only says status was considered; no finding it reduced sentence

crime_highlights: One member of the group had a knife which he held to B.M.’s throat.
The group kicked and punched the complainant.
B.M. was unconscious and having seizures when police arrived on the scene.
He also sustained permanent brain injury.
the complainant came as close to dying from the assault as is possible without actually dying.
rationale_highlights: Both accused were aboriginal youths with lengthy youth records.
The pre-sentence reports revealed that both have suffered tragic childhoods.
The sentencing judge gave full consideration to the appellant’s Aboriginal status and tragic upbringing.
note: Maximum sentence upheld; court only says background was considered, no mitigation stated
